hints: Evaluate the numerator and denominator carefully.
Draw the line of symmetry $y = x$ as a dashed diagonal mirror line.
Reflect the graph of $y = f(x)$ across $y = x$.
The reflected curve intersects $y = f(x)$ on $y = x$ in the third quadrant.
walkthrough: Draw the mirror line of reflection $y = x$ across the diagram.

Reflect the key features of $y = f(x)$ for $x < \frac{1}{2}$ across $y = x$:
$$\text{Vertical asymptote } x = \frac{1}{2} \implies \text{Horizontal asymptote } y = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Horizontal asymptote } y = 1 \implies \text{Vertical asymptote } x = 1$$
$$y\text{-intercept } (0, -1) \implies x\text{-intercept } (-1, 0)$$
$$x\text{-intercept } \left(-\frac{1}{2}, 0\right) \implies y\text{-intercept } \left(0, -\frac{1}{2}\right)$$
Sketch the reflected curve $y = f^{-1}(x)$ intersecting $y = f(x)$ on the line $y = x$.

hints: Collect terms in $x$: $x(2y - 2) = y + 1$, and divide.
The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$: examine the horizontal asymptote $y = 1$ for $x < \frac{1}{2}$ to get $x < 1$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = f(x)$ and cross-multiply to isolate $x$:
$$y = \frac{2x + 1}{2x - 1} \implies y(2x - 1) = 2x + 1 \implies 2xy - y = 2x + 1$$

Collect all terms containing $x$ on one side and factorise:
$$2xy - 2x = y + 1 \implies 2x(y - 1) = y + 1 \implies x = \frac{y + 1}{2(y - 1)}$$

Swap variables to express the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$:
$$f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x + 1}{2(x - 1)} \quad \left(\text{or } \frac{1}{x-1} + \frac{1}{2}\right)$$

Determine the domain of $f^{-1}$ from the range of $f(x)$ for $x < \frac{1}{2}$:
$$\text{Domain of } f^{-1}: x < 1$$

Evaluate the composite value $g(f(1/4))$ using $g(x) = 2x - 1$:
$$g\left(f\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\right) = g(-3) = 2(-3) - 1 = -7$$
